# FeedbackCard

A rating and comment prompt for collecting feedback on the wayfinding experience.

- **Import:** `import { FeedbackCard } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Core
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/platform-feedbackcard--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import { FeedbackCard, ThemeProvider } from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function FeedbackCardExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <FeedbackCard
        className="w-[360px]"
        title="Rate your visit"
        description="How was your route today?"
        onSubmitFeedback={(rating, comment) =>
          console.log("feedback", { rating, comment })
        }
      />
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## FeedbackCard

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `FeedbackCardProps`, which extends `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`.

- `surface`: `SurfaceVariant`, optional, default `"solid"`.

  What the card sits on: solid by default, glass where the product asks for it.

- `title`: `string`, optional, default `"Rate your experience"`.
- `description`: `string`, optional, default `"How was your navigation today?"`.
- `onSubmitFeedback`: `(rating: number, comment: string) => void`, optional.
- `isSubmitting`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.
- `successMessage`: `string`, optional, default `"Thank you for the feedback!"`.
- `variant`: `RatingVariant`, optional, default `"stars"`.

  The scale. `thumbs` is the two-option form the Express Maps prompt uses —
  "Are you enjoying this?" is a yes or a no, not a mark out of five.

- `count`: `CharacterCount`, optional.

  A character count on the comment, with the product's own limits.

- `submitLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Submit Feedback"`.

  The words on the controls. They were fixed English inside the component,
  so a visitor reading Arabic or Japanese got "Submit Feedback" whatever
  the interface language — the same defect the search row had.

- `submittingLabel`: `string`, optional, default `"Submitting..."`.
- `commentPlaceholder`: `string`, optional, default `"Tell us more about your experience..."`.
- `titleLevel`: `2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, optional, default `3`.

  The heading level the card's title takes. A card can be a section of a
  page or the whole of a dialog, and the level has to follow whatever
  heading sits above it.

- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## Types these props take

### SurfaceVariant

From `@kozmos-ds/react`.

```ts
/**
 * What a surface is made of. Solid — the background colour with the subtle
 * border — is the default everywhere; glass, the glass surface role composed
 * from `Semantics.Effect.glass`, is a choice a product makes per surface.
 */
type SurfaceVariant = "solid" | "glass";
```

### RatingVariant

From `@kozmos-ds/react`.

```ts
/**
 * What a rating is measured on.
 *
 * `stars` is an ordinal scale: choosing four means "at least four", so four
 * fill. `thumbs` is a choice between two, and exactly the one chosen fills —
 * a thumbs-up is not "two thumbs". The value is still a number so a product
 * stores one shape either way: **0 is unanswered, 1 is down, 2 is up**, which
 * is the same "1 is the lowest" rule the stars follow.
 */
type RatingVariant = "stars" | "thumbs";
```

### CharacterCount

From `@kozmos-ds/react`, which does not export it by name.

```ts
/**
 * A field's character count, and what it means.
 *
 * `limit` is a SOFT maximum, not the `maxLength` attribute. A browser refuses
 * the keystroke past `maxLength`, so with it set the "513/512, maximum
 * character limit exceeded" state in the MAP-474 feedback flow could never
 * happen — a visitor pasting a long answer would silently lose the end of it
 * instead of being told. The limit is drawn and judged here; nothing is
 * prevented.
 *
 * `minimum` is only applied once something has been typed. An empty field is
 * not yet wrong, it is unanswered, and telling someone their answer is too
 * short before they have started is noise.
 */
interface CharacterCount {
  limit: number;
  minimum?: number;
  /** Localisable. The default is the bare `52/512` the prototype draws. */
  label?: (count: number, limit: number) => string;
  overLimit?: string;
  underMinimum?: (minimum: number) => string;
}
```
